topic: AWS Certified Generative AI Developer - Professional (AIP-C01) certification exam preparation
cert_name: AWS Certified Generative AI Developer - Professional
exam_format: 65 scored questions (plus 10 unscored), 170 minutes, passing score 750/1000, compensatory scoring
question_types: multiple choice, multiple response, ordering, matching, case study
audience: Developers with 1+ years building GenAI applications on AWS who want the first professional-level AWS certification dedicated to generative AI. Ideal next step after AWS AI Practitioner (AIF-C01). Working knowledge of Python and AWS APIs assumed.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Domain 1: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
domains.notes: HEAVIEST DOMAIN. Bedrock model selection and invocation (Converse API, InvokeModel), multimodal FMs, embeddings and vector stores (OpenSearch Serverless, Aurora pgvector, S3 Vectors), data ingestion/chunking strategies for RAG, Knowledge Bases, data residency and compliance, prompt/completion logging, cross-region inference

domains.name: Domain 2: Implementation and Integration
domains.notes: Bedrock Agents and multi-agent collaboration, action groups, tool use / function calling, agentic patterns (ReAct, orchestration), Step Functions and Lambda integration, streaming responses, session/memory management, structured output, API gateway patterns, frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, Strands) on AWS

domains.name: Domain 3: AI Safety, Security, and Governance
domains.notes: Bedrock Guardrails (content filters, denied topics, contextual grounding, PII), prompt injection defense, IAM least-privilege for GenAI apps, KMS encryption, VPC endpoints/PrivateLink, model invocation logging, CloudTrail auditing, responsible AI, watermarking and provenance

domains.name: Domain 4: Operational Efficiency and Optimization for GenAI Applications
domains.notes: Cost optimization: on-demand vs provisioned throughput vs batch inference, prompt caching, model distillation, intelligent prompt routing, latency optimization, token budgeting, right-sizing model choice per task, caching strategies

domains.name: Domain 5: Testing, Validation, and Troubleshooting
domains.notes: Model evaluation (Bedrock Evaluations, LLM-as-a-judge), RAG evaluation (retrieval precision/groundedness), prompt regression testing, A/B testing, troubleshooting throttling/quota errors, debugging agent traces, CloudWatch metrics and alarms for GenAI workloads

extra_guidance: This is AWS's first professional-level GenAI certification, launched in 2026 - position as the definitive first-mover prep and the natural next step after AIF-C01. Professional level means scenario-heavy: every chapter needs realistic production scenarios with trade-off decisions (cost vs latency vs quality). Use current Bedrock model families and current API names (Converse API). Include Python/boto3 code in labs. Final chapter must be a full 65-question exam simulation walkthrough with professional-exam time strategy.
